title: Heroes' Organ Kufstein Fortress
name: Heroes' Organ Kufstein Fortress
kurzbeschreibung: The Heldenorgel at Festung Kufstein: with 4,948 pipes the world's largest open-air organ, heard daily at 12:00 noon across the entire town.
beschreibung:
Overview

The world-famous Heldenorgel at the monumental Festung Kufstein is one of Austria's most melodious and captivating cultural monuments. Housed in the fortress's fortified Bürgerturm atop a steep limestone cliff above the Inn River at around 500 metres above sea level, the instrument featuring 4,948 pipes and 65 stops ranks as the largest open-air organ in the world. Every day at 12:00 noon, its powerful sound resonates across the historic old town of Kufstein, the Inntal, and far into the slopes of the Kaisergebirge mountain range.

Route & Requirements

The Heldenorgel was constructed in 1931 by the renowned organ builder Walcker as a sounding memorial for peace and in memory of the fallen soldiers of the First World War. Over the decades, this monumental musical instrument was expanded several times and technically modernized: most recently in 2009, the organ underwent comprehensive restoration and was upgraded with a modern, mobile four-manual console. A unique feature of the engineering: the pipe chamber is located on the top floor of the Bürgerturm, while the organist performs in the fortress courtyard at the foot of the tower – a technical tour de force, as the acoustic transmission is controlled over great distances completely without delay. The daily repertoire ranges from classical masterpieces by Johann Sebastian Bach to contemporary compositions and traditionally includes the anthem "Der gute Kamerad". Every day, thousands of visitors listen to this impressive open-air concert in the fortress courtyard or along the riverside promenades of the Inn.

Visit & Arrival

The daily organ concert of the Heldenorgel takes place year-round every day at 12:00 noon (with an additional concert at 18:00 during the summer months of July and August) and lasts approximately 15 to 20 minutes. The music can be heard free of charge throughout the entire town of Kufstein; enjoying the live performance right by the console in the fortress courtyard requires an admission ticket to Festung Kufstein. Fortress admission (season 2025/2026): adults approx. €14.50, seniors approx. €13.00, children/students approx. €8.50, family ticket approx. €31.00. By public transport: ÖBB/long-distance trains to Kufstein Hauptbahnhof, from where it is just a five-minute walk across the main square to the fortress lift (Panoramabahn). By car: Inntalautobahn A12, exit Kufstein Nord or Süd, parking available in the multi-storey car parks Arkadenplatz or Zentrum.

Tips

The organ console in the fortress courtyard is barrier-free and accessible via the glass Panoramabahn inclined elevator. The finest acoustics and clear view of the console are enjoyed from the wooden benches in the covered fortress courtyard or on the panoramic terrace of the fortress restaurant.
